attachments.beat_text: Jericho’s fall in Joshua is the entry climax after the wilderness — attach this beat to the existing Tell es-Sultan dig; do not add a second Jericho pin.
attachments.caveats: Tell es-Sultan is the right tell; dating of the destruction layer relative to a Late Bronze conquest remains debated among archaeologists. Panel should present Scripture claim + dig honesty, not fake consensus.

attachments.beat_text: Ai narrative (defeat then victory) attaches to existing et-Tell candidate pin — site identification vs Khirbet el-Maqatir alternatives stays in caveats.
attachments.caveats: et-Tell identification is contested; do not treat this pin as settled Ai.

attachments.beat_text: Samaria fell and northern Israelites were deported toward Halah, Habor/Gozan, and the cities of the Medes — open the Assyrian deportation route from this pin.
attachments.caveats: Capital identification strong; exact deportee roadbeds schematic. Herodian Sebaste is later overlay.

attachments.beat_text: Lachish under Sennacherib (701) — siege documented by tell + Assyrian reliefs; connects Judah campaign branch of the deportation/campaign route.
attachments.caveats: Strong for 701 siege geography; not identical to later Babylonian operations.

attachments.beat_text: Nineveh as Assyrian imperial heartland endpoint/origin for campaign and deportation storytelling.
attachments.caveats: City identification strong; Jonah narrative geography is separate (optional/deferred as weak path).

attachments.beat_text: Babylon as exile destination for 597/586 waves and later return origin — pair with exile/return route layers.
attachments.caveats: Site strong; prophet settings are narrative loci on/near the dig, not separate invented towns.

attachments.beat_text: City of David ridge for Jerusalem under Assyrian threat (701) and Babylonian destruction/exile (586).
attachments.caveats: Distinguish 701 deliverance narrative from 586 destruction — same ridge, different outcomes.

attachments.beat_text: Mizpah as post-586 administration locale after Jerusalem’s fall.
attachments.caveats: Tell en-Nasbeh is the leading scholarly candidate for Mizpah of Benjamin.

attachments.beat_text: Cyrus Cylinder findspot packaging at Babylon — Persian policy context for the return, not a substitute for Ezra’s decree text.
attachments.caveats: Extra-biblical artifact illuminates Persian royal ideology; do not claim it is the biblical decree manuscript.

attachments.beat_text: Bethlehem start for Holy Family flight path (Matthew 2) — path layer, not a new nativity dig.
attachments.caveats: Church of the Nativity complex is early Christian tradition over the birth narrative locus — dig honesty stays on the existing pin.

attachments.beat_text: Heliopolis/On district as a cautious regional proxy for the Egyptian sojourn on the Holy Family path.
attachments.caveats: No excavated 'Holy Family house' here; later Christian traditions cluster in Delta/Old Cairo districts. Regional waypoint only.

attachments.beat_text: Nazareth return/upbringing endpoint for the Holy Family path.
attachments.caveats: Existing Nazareth house-tradition digs — do not duplicate pins.

attachments.beat_text: Golgotha crucifixion + traditional burial/resurrection packaging — Passion path endpoint; no separate tomb dig pin on map.
attachments.caveats: Traditional Calvary/Holy Sepulchre packaging vs alternate proposals (including Garden Tomb) — keep contested; path uses this existing pin.

attachments.beat_text: Olivet/Gethsemane arrest beat on the Passion path (already a miracle pin for Malchus).
attachments.caveats: Gethsemane traditional locale on Olivet slopes; exact garden footprint not surveyed as a single dig feature.

attachments.beat_text: Caiaphas family ossuary locus supports the priestly name in the Passion narrative — not a certified trial-house dig.
attachments.caveats: Historicity of Caiaphas family strong via ossuary; spatial ID of the Gospel trial is separate and unsettled.

attachments.beat_text: Pi-Ramesses dig as the Exodus route start node (with EW-01).
attachments.caveats: Strong for Rameses/Qantir identification; linking the full wilderness GPS remains mixed/debated downstream.

attachments.beat_text: Yam Suph crossing debate node — open alternate Exodus branch toggles from here.
attachments.caveats: Representative pin only; Ballah / Suez / Aqaba theories remain open.

attachments.beat_text: Traditional Sinai (Jebel Musa) on the main Exodus route — alternates documented in branch layers.
attachments.caveats: Traditional Byzantine identification; ABR/AiG and other candidates exist — use branch layers.

attachments.beat_text: Ur as Abraham migration start — attach optional patriarchal route.
attachments.caveats: Ur dig strong; patriarchal chronology vs strata debate remains.

attachments.beat_text: Susa start for Nehemiah’s return branch.
attachments.caveats: City identification strong; road to Jerusalem is schematic.
